What

What Firewood Delivery Actually Involves

Firewood isn't just a truckload dumped in your driveway. Here's what a proper Roubic firewood order looks like — from the tree it came off to the wood stacked at your storage area.

Firewood is measured in cords, and the terminology causes a lot of confusion. A full cord is 128 cubic feet, typically stacked 4 feet wide × 4 feet tall × 8 feet long. A half cord is 64 cubic feet. A face cord is roughly 42–45 cubic feet — a 4-foot-tall × 8-foot-wide stack of 16–18-inch pieces, one row deep — and it's the most common residential order, enough to last most fireplaces 4–6 weeks of regular use in heating season. Roubic delivers oak (densest, hottest, longest burn), maple (balanced, easy to start), cherry (aromatic, ideal for fire pits and pizza ovens), ash (easy to split, dries fast), and mixed hardwood blends — all seasoned 6–12 months minimum, with oak typically 12+ months for sub-20% moisture content.

What If You Buy Cheap Wood

The Cost of the Wrong Firewood

Two real problems ride along with unseasoned, out-of-region firewood — moisture and EAB. Here's what each one actually costs you.

Creosote & Chimney Fire

Green wood over 20% moisture burns inefficiently and produces far more creosote buildup in the chimney — the leading cause of chimney fires.

Cold, Damp Fires

Unseasoned wood produces lingering smoke rather than heat. Buy it in December and you're guaranteed cold, damp fires all winter.

Two to Three Seasons to Dry

Green wood needs 2–3 full heating seasons to dry in your woodshed. Money spent on wet wood is money you can't burn this year.

EAB Quarantine Violation

Out-of-county or out-of-state firewood can carry emerald ash borer larvae and violate the Ohio Department of Agriculture's EAB quarantine rules.

Spreading Emerald Ash Borer

Moving firewood across county lines is how EAB spreads to canopy that hasn't been infested yet. Locally sourced wood keeps you compliant.

Running Out Mid-Winter

Order late in a January cold snap and you pay premium pricing — if stock allows. We can run out of premium oak by mid-winter in heavy-demand years.

Common Firewood Questions

Firewood Delivery FAQ

Seven answers before you order — cord sizes, species, seasoning, EAB, and delivery.

How much is a cord of firewood in Cleveland?
Roubic seasoned hardwood firewood runs $175–$250 per face cord, $250–$400 per half cord, and $400–$650 per full cord delivered. Premium oak adds $50–$100 over mixed-hardwood pricing. Stacking adds $50–$100. Delivery is free within 10 miles of the Auburn Township yard; longer distances run $25–$75.
What's the difference between a face cord and a full cord?
A full cord is 128 cubic feet, typically stacked 4 feet wide × 4 feet tall × 8 feet long. A face cord is approximately 42–45 cubic feet — a 4-foot-tall × 8-foot-wide stack of 16–18-inch pieces, one row deep. A face cord is roughly one-third of a full cord. A face cord is the most common residential order and lasts a fireplace 4–6 weeks of regular use during heating season.
What kind of wood burns the hottest?
Oak burns the hottest and longest — densest hardwood, slow steady burn, ideal for wood stoves and overnight fires. Maple is balanced — easier to start, slightly less BTU per cord than oak. Cherry is aromatic and burns hot but faster — better for fire pits and pizza ovens than for primary heating. Ash is easy to split and dries fast, slightly less BTU than oak. Mixed hardwood blends combine the qualities of multiple species.
How do I know if firewood is seasoned?
Three checks. First, moisture meter reading — sub-20% is well-seasoned, 20–25% is acceptable, over 25% is unseasoned. A meter costs about $20 at any hardware store. Second, visual signs — ends of the pieces show radial cracks (checks), and bark separates easily from the wood. Third, weight and sound — seasoned wood is noticeably lighter than green wood and produces a hollow ringing sound when two pieces are knocked together. Roubic firewood is seasoned 6–12 months minimum.
Why does locally sourced firewood matter (EAB)?
Emerald Ash Borer is an invasive beetle that has killed an estimated 90%+ of ash trees in NE Ohio since 2008. The Ohio Department of Agriculture maintains an EAB quarantine — firewood from infested counties shouldn't move across county lines because EAB larvae can survive in the wood and infest new areas. Buying locally sourced firewood (within the same county where the wood was cut) keeps you compliant and helps slow the spread to areas that haven't been infested yet.
Do you deliver and stack firewood?
Yes. Delivery is included in the cord price; the wood is dumped at your driveway or designated drop point. Stacking at your wood-storage area is an add-on at $50–$100 depending on distance from the drop point. Tell us during the order whether you want stacking — it's the most-requested add-on.
When should I order firewood, and how much will I need?
Order in August or early September for fall delivery — stock is abundant, pricing is stable, and the wood has time to settle before the first cold snap. Emergency orders during a January cold snap are filled when stock allows but trend toward premium pricing. For volume: homes heating primarily with a wood stove typically use 3–6 full cords per season, while fireplace-only aesthetic use runs 1–2 face cords per season.
